title: Automation Bias and Deskilling in Radiology AI: A Confidence-stratified Triage Model for Workflow Integration.
desc: [Radiology. Artificial intelligence] Radiology is adopting artificial intelligence (AI) faster than it is studying what AI does to radiologists' perceptual expertise and interpretive skill. The question has partly shifted from whether these tools perform well on benchmark tasks to what happens to clinical judgment when use of these tools becomes routine. Two risks accompany this transition: automation bias, the tendency to follow AI suggestions without adequate scrutiny, and deskilling, the erosion of perceptual and interpretive ability through disuse, typically revealed when AI support is withdrawn. Incorrect AI output degrades accuracy regardless of experience, the benefit of assistance varies unpredictably across readers and tasks, and performance falls after AI withdrawal; neither risk has been studied longitudinally in radiology. A confidence-stratified triage model is proposed in which calibrated AI confidence, not findings alone, routes cases to low-, intermediate-, or high-confidence streams: output withheld until independent reading, shown with uncertainty signals and a checklist, or shown with random blinded audit. Demonstrated local confidence calibration is a precondition for deployment, and stream thresholds and audit rates should be weighted by task and potential clinical harm, not error probability alone. Rather than applying one workflow to every case, the model redistributes radiologist attention to where AI error is most likely and most consequential, operationalizing four principles: keeping the radiologist in the decision loop, making AI uncertainty visible, inserting targeted cognitive friction, and governing the human-AI interaction as a system. A research agenda to determine whether these countermeasures reduce automation bias and skill erosion in practice is also proposed.

title: Development, validation and AI chatbot evaluation of the Adolescent Mental Health AI Response Tool

Applying AMHART to four widely used AI chatbots revealed that these models have greater coverage for anxiety than depression and for moderate than severe presentations, also identifying gaps for coping guidance.

title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
desc: [Frontiers in oncology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monitoring. A key focus is on integrating AI with multi-omics data, including proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to support precision oncology and personalized treatments. We address important validation challenges, like model interpretability, data quality, and regulatory issues that must be solved before AI can be widely used in clinics. By summarizing current evidence and targeting research gaps, this review offers a clear view of how AI is enhancing the discovery, personalization, and validation of anticancer treatments.

title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
desc: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

title: Richer database context improves LLM-generated EHR phenotyping algorithms
desc: Objective: To evaluate large language model (LLM) generation of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) phenotyping SQL and the effect of database implementation context. Materials and Methods: Eight publicly accessible LLM-based systems generated SQL under progressively richer prompts using synthetic and University of North Carolina (UNC) Health electronic health record (EHR) data, both based on the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) model. Outputs were compared with the Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE) T2DM reference phenotype using SQL executability, F1, positive predictive value (PPV), and recall. Results: Fewer than 55% of limited-context synthetic outputs and no limited-context UNC EHR outputs executed without modification. Detailed codebooks (L3) increased executability to 81.3% in synthetic OMOP and 100% in UNC EHR; adding sample rows (L4) increased synthetic executability to 100%. Limited-context recall was as low as 0.01, whereas high-context outputs achieved recall [≥]0.99 at synthetic L4 and >0.90 at UNC L3, although UNC PPV remained substantially lower than recall. At the highest available context levels, Beta F1 ranged from 0.72-0.99 in synthetic OMOP and 0.57-0.68 in UNC EHR; all UNC models exceeded the diagnosis-code baseline (F1=0.54). The top synthetic performer fell from F1=0.99 to 0.64 on UNC EHR. Discussion: Richer database context was associated with more consistent SQL executability and recall, while model rankings varied across datasets. Conclusion: LLMs can generate clinically meaningful T2DM phenotyping SQL when provided with sufficient database context, but limited PPV in real-world data underscores the need for local validation.

title: Verifiable Agentic Science on Public Infrastructure
desc: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents are transforming the practice of science. Across every discipline, researchers are handing data analysis to coding agents that can design and execute complex studies from a single prompt. Yet this revolution carries a threat. When agents improvise in local environments, they leave no verifiable record, ultimately risking a wave of irreproducible science. Solving this crisis requires moving agentic science onto public infrastructure where every action leaves an examinable trail. Here we connect autonomous coding agents to shared computing resources, turning ephemeral prompts into auditable scientific records. After showing that 30 unguided local agents splinter into 18 incompatible pipelines on the same dataset, we conduct an agentic reproduction and discovery study on a large scale---reproducing a large, diverse array of studies with every workflow, history, and intermediate dataset publicly accessible. This complete provenance trail exposes unstated modeling choices, reference mismatches, and subsampled tutorial inputs in published studies, and establishes a new foundation where human scientists can understand, steer, and trust AI-driven discovery.

title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Chronic Hepatitis B.
source: PubMed · Journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
desc: [Journal of gastroenterology and hepatology] Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) burdens the healthcare system, affecting millions of individuals worldwide with a potential progression to complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The World Health Organization launched the chronic viral hepatitis elimination plan which aimed to eliminate chronic hepatitis B virus by 2030, yet the goal has seemed to be far from reach with the remaining few years owing to different hurdles ranging from screening strategy and diagnosis to risk stratification for antiviral treatment and HCC surveillance. To refine the management of CHB, previous studies focused on identifying the at-risk populations and predictors for adverse outcomes using conventional statistical methods. With the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI), there is further room to improve different aspects of screening and management. For instance, generative AI, such as large language models (LLMs), has been proven to have the ability to answer different clinical questions, assisting patients' and physicians' decision on various clinical scenarios. Different machine learning and deep learning models have also been developed to assess for liver fibrosis, as well as to aid segmentation of liver structures and detection of focal liver lesions through various imaging modalities. While different AI models have shown superior performance compared to those developed through traditional statistical models, the lack of standardized datasets in training cohorts and the unresolved concerns of hallucination of false information in LLMs pose challenges on applying AI in the current management of CHB, in which further studies are required to adopt AI into daily clinical practice.

title: EM-BENCH: A Reproducible Framework for Benchmarking Guideline-Concordant Clinical Decision Making in Large Language Models
desc: Background Physicians increasingly use artificial intelligence tools to support clinical work, yet there is no accepted standard for measuring the competency of large language models (LLMs) in clinical decision support. We developed EM-BENCH, a physician-validated, deterministically scored benchmark for evaluating whether models reliably apply the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) guidelines to clinical decisions. Methods EM-BENCH comprises 210 binary clinical vignettes covering all 70 critical questions across 25 ACEP clinical policies. We evaluated 149 LLM configurations representing 79 base models using prespecified answers and deterministic scoring. Each vignette had a prespecified correct answer to a binary yes-or-no question based on an ACEP recommendation. We examined associations between accuracy and model access tier (closed-access vs. open-weight models), model size, release date, clinical policy, recommendation evidence level, and reasoning settings. Results No configuration achieved complete guideline concordance. The highest performing configuration answered 207 of 210 vignettes correctly (98.6%). Closed-access models outperformed open-weight models (median accuracy, 91% vs. 63%; Hodges-Lehmann location shift, 26 percentage points; 99% CI, 20 to 33; adjusted P<0.001). Among open-weight model families, a 10-fold increase in parameter count was associated with a 14-percentage-point increase in accuracy (99% CI, 7.7 to 20; adjusted P<0.001). Across all models, accuracy increased by 8.9 percentage points per release year (99% CI, 3.6 to 14; adjusted P<0.001). Neither enabling a thinking mode (pseudomedian change, 0.95 percentage points; 99% CI, -2.6 to 3.1; adjusted P=1.00) nor high versus low reasoning effort (0.91 percentage points; 99% CI, -0.69 to 3.1; adjusted P=0.56) consistently improved accuracy. Conclusions Contemporary LLMs showed improving but incomplete ability to apply ACEP guidelines. Concordance varied markedly across models and was associated with access tier, size, and release recency, while additional inference-time reasoning offered inconsistent benefit. Specialty-specific, physician-validated benchmarks may provide a reproducible assessment of LLMs' ability to make guideline-concordant clinical decisions.

title: PepPr: De Novo peptide sequencing with peptide priors
desc: Mass spectrometry-based peptide sequencing underpins proteomics. Database search confines to predefined candidates, whereas de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) struggles with incomplete spectra. Existing hybrid methods use databases only for post hoc correction or retrieve previously identified spectra to guide decoding. We instead combine DNPS with a peptide prior: a language model fitted to a reference proteome, tolerating variants yet uncertain on strongly divergent sequences. Relative to prior-free DNPS, our implementation, PepPr, improved reference peptide identification and improved rather than suppressed variant identification. Using a related proteome as prior, it matched or outperformed homology-driven database search, and its gain over prior-free DNPS grew with relatedness. In antibody sequencing, it improved recovery of peptides spanning the variable-constant boundary, deamidation calls, and assembly, while preserving recall of hypervariable regions inaccessible to database search. Peptide priors thus bring reference knowledge into DNPS without limiting discovery.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Cataract Surgery: A Review of Preoperative, Intraoperative and Postoperative Applications.
desc: [Clinical & experimental ophthalmology] Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in the fields of medicine and ophthalmology. Recent advances in machine learning, deep learning and convolutional neural networks have significantly improved cataract detection and grading, intraocular lens power calculations, surgical decision-making, risk prediction and patient education. Intraoperative AI-assisted surgical phase recognition, workflow analysis, real-time guidance, robotic technologies and femtosecond laser integration can improve surgical precision, efficiency and safety. AI has shown promise in predicting visual outcomes, detecting postoperative complications and facilitating telemedicine follow-up. Though challenges with AI include transparency, data diversity, regulatory oversight and clinical validation, continued advances are expected to further personalise cataract surgery, support clinical decision-making, optimise surgical performance and improve patient outcomes. This narrative summarises the current and emerging applications of AI in preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative management of cataracts.

title: VascFlux-GEO: Comparator selection and auditability in vascular transcriptome module prediction
desc: Background: Mathematical coupling and comparator selection are established concerns when a transcriptome response is defined as follow-up minus baseline. We assessed whether apparent within-cohort improvement survives matched constant-follow-up and scalar-shrinkage controls, and whether specified evaluation faults are detectable in an auditable vascular transcriptome benchmark. Results: Using eight frozen modules, 72 rosuvastatin pairs, 14 peripheral artery disease pairs, 20 repeated subject-held-out five-fold partitions, and 5,000 subject bootstrap draws of fixed losses, we compared 15 explicit specifications. Supporting post hoc analyses included 800 known-truth training/test simulations, annotation and input-ablation sensitivities, complete-tuning integrity checks, and an independent-source cross-sectional artery description. In GSE86216, nested follow-up ridge had lower observed repeated-CV mean absolute error than mean follow-up, 0.3280 versus 0.3405 (difference 0.0126; descriptive central 95% percentile range 0.0033-0.0224), while scalar shrinkage had lower observed error (0.3256). These ranges have no validated coverage guarantee. No full-matrix advantage was established; equivalence was not tested. In peripheral artery disease, nested ridge (0.3449) had slightly higher observed MAE than the median follow-up comparator (0.3409), and no advantage was established. Simulations illustrated how mean follow-up can outperform mean change without temporal signal, while the GSE281841 histological stenosis-grade description remained limited by anatomical imbalance, unconfirmed participant identity and an unresolved sample-count discrepancy. Conclusions: These retrospective, nonconfirmatory comparisons show modestly lower observed within-cohort error than constant-follow-up controls in one cohort, without established full-matrix advantage. They do not partition prediction into mathematical, technical and biological components. Independent longitudinal validation and clinical utility remain unestablished.

title: Innovation and AI in Endourology: An Overview from EAU Endourology.
desc: [Current urology reports] Advancements in technology have been at the heart of endourology for decades. With the introduction of new and novel technologies, endourology is rapidly changing. This review aims to address the recent innovations and technological advances in endourology by addressing four different areas where tangible outcome improvements are being seen: (1) diagnostic and detection methods; (2) intraoperative optimisation and procedural automation; (3) prediction of treatment outcomes; and (4) the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for patients' education and monitoring. AI applications in endourology consistently demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy, with stone detection rates exceeding 95% across imaging modalities. Emerging tools include non-invasive analysis of stone composition and real-time intraoperative segmentation. Intraoperative improvements involve augmented reality-guided renal access, which has reduced puncture times, fluoroscopy exposure, and complications. New instruments, such as flexible, navigable suction devices (FANS) and intrarenal pressure (IRP) and temperature (IRT) monitoring systems, bring the field closer to achieving the endourological quadrifecta. Machine learning models trained on multicentre data can predict perioperative risks and personalise treatment, demonstrating similar effectiveness in managing stone disease. Additionally, generative AI and large language models are increasingly used for clinical documentation, patient communication, and outpatient workflows. However, concerns about hallucination, data privacy, and the need for human oversight remain significant in this growing area. Innovation, technology, and AI in endourology are advancing rapidly, introducing new ideas that are integrated into surgical procedures. These innovations offer numerous benefits to patients at various stages of treatment, leading to improved surgical results. Although combining these technologies can potentially maximise patient benefits, a careful and selective approach should be adopted, accompanied by thorough assessments before implementing these new innovations.

title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
desc: Peer review is the principal quality control of published research, but methodological errors can go undetected. In an earlier experiment with errors inserted into three reports of randomized clinical trials, untrained human reviewers achieved a mean major-error detection score of 27%. Here, we tested whether 15 large language models (LLMs), including four open-weight models, detect the same errors. Their major-error detection scores ranged from 53% to 96%. To reduce the risk of memorization, we repeated the test on three clinical trials published in 2026. Scores ranged from 51% to 99%, and from 66% to 87% for the open-weight models. Notably, LLMs still flagged 2% to 29% of the error types in control reports without inserted errors, most often conclusions not supported by the results and missing reasons why screened patients were not enrolled. Across the 12 models, mean review times ranged from 1.4 to 16.3 minutes. Opus 5.5 achieved the highest major-error detection score (99%), while GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna offered cost-effective alternatives with scores of 92% and 87%, respectively. Together, these tests provide a benchmark for specialized review models and suggest that relying on human peer review alone may leave avoidable methodological errors undetected.

The use of biological age and artificial intelligence in health care.
desc: [npj aging] This commentary highlights the age illusion and advocates integrating biological age and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance clinical precision in health care. By synthesizing geroscience and machine learning, practitioners and scientists can effectively bridge the gap between experimental biomarkers and personalized medicine and longevity care. This contribution is timely as the importance of biological age and predictive analytics offer transformative potential for diagnostics while necessitating a focus on modern medical systems. This article aims to elucidate how AI accelerates the clinical implementation of biological age rather than current chronological age in precision medicine.

Artificial intelligence in digital implant dentistry: current applications, clinical translation, and future directions.
desc: [Odontology] Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly expanded across digital implant dentistry, with applications ranging from diagnosis and treatment planning to surgical execution, prosthetic rehabilitation, outcome prediction, and biomechanical optimization. However, the clinical readiness and translational value of many proposed AI systems remain uncertain. This comprehensive state-of-the-art narrative review aims to provide an integrated overview of AI applications throughout the implant workflow while critically evaluating current evidence, methodological limitations, and challenges to clinical implementation. A comprehensive narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by Google Scholar and manual reference screening. The review was prepared according to SANRA recommendations. AI has demonstrated promising performance in automated image analysis, implant planning, computer-assisted surgery, prosthetic workflows, implant identification, peri-implant disease detection, predictive modelling, and biomechanical optimization. Nevertheless, most available evidence is derived from retrospective studies, simulation-based investigations, or single-center datasets. Limited external validation, heterogeneity in study design, and insufficient prospective clinical evidence continue to restrict widespread clinical adoption. Furthermore, improvements in technical performance do not necessarily translate into superior patient-centered outcomes. AI has the potential to enhance efficiency, consistency, and clinical decision support throughout the implant workflow. However, current evidence supports its role primarily as an adjunctive tool rather than an autonomous clinical system. Future progress will depend on robust validation, standardized reporting, explainable AI frameworks, and prospective clinical studies demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes. Clinical Relevance Statement: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in the digital implant workflow, from radiographic analysis and virtual patient construction to computer-assisted surgery, prosthetic design, and outcome prediction. This review helps clinicians distinguish the AI-specific components of these technologies from conventional digital tools, identify which applications are supported by clinical evidence versus those that remain experimental, and understand the current limitations regarding validation, generali

Artificial intelligence readiness profiles associated with critical thinking among nursing interns: A latent profile analysis.
desc: [Nurse education today] To identify distinct profiles of artificial intelligence (AI) readiness among nursing interns, to explore the relationship between these profiles and critical thinking ability, and to examine the factors associated with profile membership. The integration of AI into healthcare and nursing education necessitates that nursing students develop AI readiness. Critical thinking is a core competency for clinical decision-making and professional practice. Understanding how AI readiness profiles relate to critical thinking can inform tailored educational interventions. A cross-sectional survey study. A total of 458 nursing interns were recruited via convenience sampling from a teaching hospital in China. Data were collected using the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale and the Simplified Critical Thinking Scale. Latent profile analysis (LPA) and multinomial logistic regression were performed. Three distinct AI readiness profiles were identified: "Cognition-Deficient Type" (35.6%), "Moderately Balanced Type" (48.0%), and "Comprehensive Excellence Type" (16.4%). Critical thinking scores differed significantly across profiles (p < 0.001), with higher AI readiness associated with stronger critical thinking ability. In terms of other related variables, there were significant differences between the groups in terms of satisfaction with the nursing profession, exposure to AI-medicine interdisciplinary course, attitude towards AI application in healthcare (p < 0.001). Nursing interns exhibit heterogeneous AI readiness levels, which are positively associated with critical thinking. Tailored educational strategies should be developed to enhance both AI readiness and critical thinking skills.

Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use and Objective Documentation Effort Among Emergency Physicians.
desc: [Annals of emergency medicine] Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes ("AI scribes") are purported to reduce emergency department (ED) documentation burden, but ED evidence is largely single-site, uncontrolled, or self-reported, with exposure inferred rather than measured. We evaluated AI scribe use among attending emergency physicians across a multisite network, with exposure and outcomes read directly from the electronic health record. Across 20 EDs (3 academic and 17 community), AI scribe use was flagged per note from the patient consent statement within the ED note. Analyses were restricted to attending physicians and, to isolate the physician's own documentation, excluded teaching encounters and attestation notes identified from standardized attestation text. Endpoints, computed over the mature-adoption window (December 2025 onward, when Epic audit-log data are retained), were active time in the note (primary), note length, note-start time, completion lag, and 72-hour ED return. Within-physician models (physician and calendar-month fixed effects, clustered by physician) compared each adopter's AI-scribed notes with their own unassisted notes, adjusting only for pre-exposure case mix. Among 275 attending physicians, 31% of encounters were AI-scribed. Physicians spent less active time in AI-scribed notes (median 10.0 versus 12.5 min-2.4 minutes after adjustment), started them about 15 minutes later (median 31 versus 17 minutes after first seeing the patient, and produced notes about 14% longer [median 5,220 versus 4,468 characters; within-physician +629 characters]). Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes), and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% confidence interval -1.5 to -0.1). Among emergency physicians, AI scribe use was associated with less active time in the note, deferred note-start, and longer notes, without delaying completion or increasing short-term returns, with effect sizes consistent with ambulatory randomized data.

title: Pharmacist-Led Medication Titration for Cardiometabolic Disease: Evidence, Equity, and Scale.
desc: [Current cardiology reports] To review community-based pharmacist-led medication titration across cardiometabolic conditions and the infrastructure needed to deliver this model at scale. This review reframes cardiometabolic medication optimization as a continuum from passive gap identification to active longitudinal medication management. Registries, dashboards, audit and feedback, electronic health record alerts, and inpatient initiation can identify undertreatment or prompt prescribing, but they do not provide infrastructure for dose adjustment, monitoring, adherence support, and medication-access navigation. Pharmacist-led, team-based models occupy the active end of this continuum. The strongest evidence is in hypertension, with meaningful blood pressure reductions; in heart failure, interdisciplinary titration programs more directly address target-dose achievement than alerts or decision-support tools. Emerging data extend this framework to diabetes, lipidology, and obesity. Value-based care provides a reimbursement framework to support these services. Pharmacist-led titration can close gaps between therapies and delivery, but scaling requires equity-focused implementation, flexible staffing, population health infrastructure that connects artificial intelligence-enabled patient identification to action, and sustainable reimbursement.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Periodontal Diseases Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review.
desc: [Oral diseases] Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have shown promise for the detection of periodontal disease. This study aimed to synthesize current evidence on the diagnostic performance of AI models applied to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) for periodontal disease. A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted to identify studies on AI-assisted diagnosis of periodontal disease using CBCT published up to December 2025. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool was used to assess the risk of bias. Among 10,099 records screened, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies indicate that AI models, predominantly based on convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures applied to CBCT images, have substantial potential for detecting periodontal bone loss and related conditions. However, diagnostic performance metrics varied markedly across studies, and direct comparisons with human clinicians produced inconsistent findings, underscoring the need for more rigorous study designs and standardized datasets. Despite limitations arising from heterogeneous methodologies and non-standardized data collection, CBCT-based AI models show considerable promise for enhancing periodontal disease diagnosis. Further high-quality, methodologically robust research is warranted to validate and optimize these approaches for clinical use. PROSPERO: CRD420251273846.

title: Alpiniae oxyphyllae Fructus in Alzheimer's Disease: Multi-Target Mechanisms, Current Evidence, and Future AI-Driven Perspectives.
desc: [Molecules (Basel, Switzerland)] Alpiniae oxyphyllae Fructus (Zingiberaceae; Alpinia oxyphylla Miq) (AOF) is a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible homologous material rich in bioactive metabolites, including flavonoids, terpenes, and sesquiterpenes. Its multiple metabolites and multi-target nature confer unique advantages for cognitive function and neuroprotection. However, recent advances in extraction techniques, the discovery of AOF effects, and novel ameliorative mechanisms against Alzheimer's disease (AD) require an updated review. This review systematically expands on the botanical features, traditional dietary applications, and quality control of AOF raw materials, as well as its AD-ameliorating effect, in vivo absorption, toxicological safety, and extraction technology optimization strategies. Moreover, we explored the emerging mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of AOF and its bioactive metabolites in improving AD, including effects on glial cell function, the gut-brain axis, brain metal ions, and advanced glycation end products. This review comprehensively summarizes preclinical studies, clinical research, and commercially available products related to AOF and its metabolites. It also expounds upon the potential impetus that artificial intelligence could offer AOF research in the future. In summary, this review provides innovative technologies, in-depth mechanistic analyses, and novel research directions for exploring AOF extracts and their bioactive metabolites to offer strategic guidance for identifying new functional factors and drug candidates to combat AD.

title: Artificial intelligence to support infant feeding and nutritional care: a scoping review.
desc: [Journal of pediatric nursing] Infant feeding and nutrition are critical for growth, development, and long-term health outcomes. As paediatric nurses play a central role in infant monitoring and feeding practices, there is growing interest in innovative approaches to support early assessment and personalised nutritional care. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly explored to support clinical decision-making; however, its applications in infant feeding and nutrition have not been comprehensively synthesised. To map AI applications in infant feeding and nutrition and examine their potential implications for clinical care and paediatric nursing practice. This scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's framework and adhered to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of research databases was conducted across seven electronic databases, grey literature, and trial registers, including studies published from inception to 26 May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and extracted and synthesised data. Twenty-nine studies were included. Seven broad AI application areas were identified: 1) prediction and classification of nutritional status, 2) estimation and monitoring of growth, 3) providing nutritional recommendations, 4) analysing nutritional practices and variations, 5) suckling and feeding behaviour analysis, 6) feeding method and behaviour monitoring, and 7) prediction and classification of feeding status. AI demonstrates potential to support paediatric nurses and healthcare professionals by enabling more timely, personalised interventions to improve nutritional care and long-term infant health outcomes. However, current evidence remains largely developmental, highlighting the need for real-world clinical studies to determine the safety, effectiveness, and integration of AI technologies into paediatric care. Open Science Framework (Registration Number: b45tv).

title: Smart livestock management using sensing technologies: applications, digital integration, and future perspectives.
source: PubMed · Tropical animal health and production
desc: [Tropical animal health and production] Smart livestock management is increasingly enabled by advances in sensing and biosensing technologies that support continuous, data-driven monitoring of animal health, welfare, reproduction, productivity, and environmental conditions. Recent digital innovations have further accelerated this transition, creating opportunities for more predictive and sustainable livestock management. This review synthesizes current knowledge on conventional sensors, emerging biosensing technologies, and their integration within smart livestock systems. It critically examines technology readiness, wearable, implantable, and environmental sensing platforms. It evaluates their applications in disease surveillance, animal welfare assessment, reproductive management, milk production optimization, and growth monitoring. The review further explores how the convergence of sensors and biosensors with the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), cloud and edge computing, and digital decision-support systems (DSS) enables continuous data integration, predictive analytics, and evidence-based management. Current barriers to large-scale implementation, including technical reliability, interoperability, data management, infrastructure requirements, economic feasibility, and regulatory and ethical considerations, are also discussed. The available evidence indicates that integrating sensing, biosensing, and digital technologies provides a more comprehensive understanding of animal physiological, behavioral, and environmental status than individual technologies alone, supporting earlier interventions and improved production efficiency. Continued advances in integrated monitoring platforms, intelligent analytics, and next-generation biosensors are expected to accelerate the transition toward predictive, resilient, and sustainable livestock production.

title: Unraveling Structure and Spectroscopic Signatures of Pt/γ-Al2O3 via an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Simulation Framework.
desc: [ACS applied materials & interfaces] Supported subnanometer clusters have attracted significant attention in catalysis. Yet, it is challenging to resolve their structural evolution, particularly in the presence of adsorbates. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled simulation framework that integrates machine learning force field (MLFF) construction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ML-assisted infrared (IR) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra analysis to investigate the restructuring of supported subnanometer clusters. Using Pt10/γ-Al2O3(110) as a model system, we explored the CO-induced restructuring of the cluster under different conditions. The simultaneous machine learning (ML)-spectra elucidate a strong interplay among adsorbate coverage, cluster restructuring, and cluster-support interaction. This work sheds light on the complex dynamics of supported subnanometer clusters that is extendible to other systems.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Neonatal Care and Research : Based on 14th Dr. I. C. Verma Excellence in Research Award Delivered as Oration on 4th October 2026.
desc: [Indian journal of pediatrics] Neonatology has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past six decades, evolving from a discipline focused predominantly on preventing neonatal death to one increasingly concerned with quality of survival, neurodevelopment, family-integrated care and long-term health. Despite substantial progress, neonatal mortality remains a major global health challenge. In 2024, approximately 2.3 million newborns died globally, with the highest mortality rates in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. India has achieved a substantial decline in neonatal mortality, from 28 to 17 per 1000 live births between 2015 and 2023, accompanied by rapid expansion of facility-based newborn care. However, prematurity, low birth weight, intrapartum complications, infection, antimicrobial resistance, inequitable access, workforce constraints and inadequate long-term follow-up remain major challenges. The epidemiology of neonatal disease is also changing, with increasing survival of extremely premature infants and greater recognition of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, retinopathy of prematurity, brain injury and developmental impairment. Neonatal research is similarly moving from descriptive epidemiology and rescue therapy towards prediction, prevention, precision medicine and implementation science. The next decade should prioritize prevention of prematurity, precision sepsis management, respiratory and brain protection, nutrition and gut health, Kangaroo Mother Care, zero separation, artificial intelligence and predictive analytics, long-term outcomes and affordable innovations. The ultimate measure of neonatal care should move beyond survival to enabling every newborn to develop and reach their full potential.

title: Ultra-early diagnosis recently developments of acute myocardial infarction: Emerging biomarkers and advanced sensing technologies.
source: PubMed · Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
desc: [Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry] Currently, myocardial infarction is commonly detected via traditional biomarker analysis, electrocardiography, and echocardiography. In general, conventional clinical approaches are limited by insufficient early-stage sensitivity and time-consuming procedures, thereby delaying therapeutic interventions. To address the above-mentioned drawbacks, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in both ultra-early biomarkers and novel high-sensitivity detection platforms. A panel of ultra-early biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity (e.g., GPBB, cMyC, cfDNA, MPO, D-dimer, miRNAs, and lncRNAs) is explicitly identified in this review. Recent progress in nano-based, graphene-based, and chemical biosensors for biomarker detection is further elaborated. The application of these biosensors delivers amplified signal outputs, enhanced sensitivity, shortened detection time, multiplex detection capability, and successful miniaturization of detection devices. This review also analyzes the integration of artificial intelligence models with conventional diagnostic modalities (electrocardiography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging) and gold-standard diagnostic methods (biomarker testing, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, coronary computed tomography). Such integrated analytical strategies enable objective, rapid, and early diagnosis. When embedde into wearable monitoring devices, these technologies support non-invasive and continuous real-time monitoring and generate preemptive clinical alerts with ultra-high signal sensitivity. Ultimately, this article establishes a comprehensive framework for the ultra-early diagnosis of myocardial infarction by integrating screened ultra-early biomarkers and innovative high-sensitivity detection techniques.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Purposes of Public Health: A Critical Look at Technology.
desc: [The Hastings Center report] Within public health, the contemporary discourse surrounding AI in this field is dominated by what this paper terms the "standard approach." In this frame, AI appears as a neutral tool to be evaluated for accuracy, privacy protection, and bias mitigation. When direct benefits outweigh direct harms, AI is described as an opportunity to improve public health practice. But the standard approach does not consider how public health's adoption of AI discloses and reinforces different accounts of the underlying purpose of the profession. Drawing insights from the communitarian thinker Wendell Berry, we demonstrate how AI does not merely improve efficiency and add capabilities but tends to align public health practice with purposes and assumptions that, when actualized, increasingly displace community power and authentic human presence. This tendency is clear in three commonly proposed applications of AI in public health practice: health education, community health assessments, and data analysis. Because the advent of AI offers an opportunity for greater technological efficiency, it offers the public health community the opportunity to reflect on what ultimate ends those efficiencies should be directed toward.

title: Any Artificial Intelligence Tool Use Experience and Depression-Anxiety Symptom Profiles Among Rural University Students in China.
source: PubMed · Psychology research and behavior management
desc: [Psychology research and behavior management] Associations of artificial intelligence (AI) tool use with concurrent depressive and anxiety symptoms among rural university students remain uncertain. We explored associations of any AI tool use experience with depression-anxiety symptom profiles. This cross-sectional survey included 1529 students with rural household registration from three universities in Zhejiang, China. GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores informed latent profile analysis; five conceptually ordered multinomial models compared profile membership with the low-symptom profile. The profiles comprised low symptoms (n=896; 58.6%), anxiety-predominant symptoms (n=587; 38.4%), and depression-predominant symptoms (n=46; 3.0%). In the reported fully adjusted model, AI use experience was associated with lower odds of anxiety-predominant membership (OR=0.764, 95% CI 0.654-0.893) and depression-predominant membership (OR=0.239, 95% CI 0.101-0.566) compared with low-symptom membership. AI use experience and symptom patterns were associated in this exploratory sample. These observations warrant longitudinal assessment with more detailed measures of AI engagement.
